clause_text: If the aggregate actual number of Details for the Product made by the Sales Representatives for a Calendar Quarter is less than the Quarterly Minimum Details for such Calendar Quarter, then in calculating the promotion fee due under Section 6.1.1, the Applicable Percentage for such Calendar Quarter shall be reduced to a new percentage equal to [***].
mapping_reason: Deal-structure/economic provision concerning how revenue or profit is split -- not a payment-timing or invoicing provision.
annotation_notes: UNFAIRNESS 0.25: the fee-adjustment mechanism runs in one direction only -- missing the Quarterly Minimum Details reduces the Applicable Percentage, with no reciprocal uplift for exceeding it in the visible text. That is a real but minor asymmetry, and performance-linked fee adjustment is normal in promotion agreements. Cannot go higher because the actual reduced percentage is redacted as '[***]' -- proportionality, which is the thing that would distinguish a mild adjustment from a punitive one, is not observable. AMBIGUITY 0.50: three defined terms ('Details', 'Quarterly Minimum Details', 'Applicable Percentage'), a cross-reference to Section 6.1.1, and the operative number itself are all outside the span. A reader of this span alone cannot determine what happens. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: no rule in indian_legal_rules.csv has a trigger_condition matching a performance-linked fee adjustment. ENFORCEABILITY 0.25: ICA_S74_01 was considered and NOT applied -- its trigger requires a sum named as payable ON BREACH, whereas this is a reduction in fee earned for services not rendered, which is a different legal construct. Residual 0.25 records that if the redacted reduction were severe enough to be characterised as a stipulated consequence of breach, the S.74 question could arise; that is unresolvable on the visible text.
ai_uncertainty_note: The redaction is decisive. Whether this clause is benign or aggressive depends entirely on the value hidden behind '[***]'. Confidence is Low for that reason alone.

clause_text: CUSTOMER SHALL RELEASE, DEFEND, INDEMNIFY AND HOLD HARMLESS TRANSPORTER AND TRANSPORTER'S MEMBERS, DIRECTORS, OFFICERS, AGENTS AND EMPLOYEES FROM AND AGAINST ANY AND ALL SUITS, ACTIONS, CAUSES OF ACTION, CLAIMS, DEMANDS, LOSSES, LIABILITIES AND EXPENSES (INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, INTEREST, COURT COSTS, REASONABLE ATTORNEYS' FEES AND EXPENSES, AND OTHER COSTS OF DEFENSE) (COLLECTIVELY, "CLAIMS") RELATING TO, CAUSED BY OR ARISING OUT OF CUSTOMER'S BREACH OF ANY REPRESENTATION, WARRANTY OR COVENANT MADE BY CUSTOMER HEREUNDER, BUT NOT TO THE PROPORTIONATE EXTENT THAT SUCH CLAIM IS CAUSED BY OR RESULTS FROM OR ARISES OUT OF THE GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OF TRANSPORTER.
mapping_reason: Restricts a party's ability to bring legal proceedings on certain matters.
legal_basis: ICA_S124_01 (Indian Contract Act ss.124-125, indemnity) was considered because the clause is substantively an indemnity, but its trigger_condition ('indemnity obligation is uncapped or unusually broad in scope') is NOT met -- see notes. No rule is asserted.
annotation_notes: CATEGORY MISMATCH -- PRIMARY FINDING. This span is assigned 'Dispute Resolution' via CUAD 'Covenant Not To Sue', but its text is a release / defend / indemnify / hold-harmless clause. It contains no forum-selection, arbitration, or bar-on-proceedings language. The assigned category does not describe the clause. UNFAIRNESS 0.50: obligations run one way only (Customer indemnifies Transporter and its members, directors, officers, agents and employees; no reciprocal obligation appears). Held at Moderate rather than High because two genuine limits are present in the text: the indemnity is confined to Claims arising from Customer's OWN breach of its representations/warranties/covenants, and it is proportionately carved back for Transporter's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Those are meaningful protections, not symbolic ones. AMBIGUITY 0.25: unusually precise for its type -- 'Claims' is expressly defined inline and the carve-out is explicit. Residual 0.25 for 'proportionate extent', which requires apportionment machinery not visible here. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: no applicable rule; ICA_S124_01 trigger not met. ENFORCEABILITY 0.25: low residual only. The gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct carve-out is precisely the feature whose ABSENCE would raise concern.
ai_uncertainty_note: Because the clause's true subject (indemnity) is not its assigned category (Dispute Resolution), the rule inventory was searched by substance rather than by category label. A human should confirm that this is the right way to resolve a category/substance conflict -- the guidelines do not currently say.
ai_guideline_issue: Guidelines do not state whether to annotate against the ASSIGNED category or the clause's ACTUAL subject matter when they conflict, nor whether an annotator may cite a rule scoped to a different category.

clause_text: This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, but without giving effect to its laws or rules relating to conflicts of laws.
annotation_notes: A clean, standard Delaware choice-of-law clause with an express exclusion of renvoi/conflicts rules. UNFAIRNESS 0.00: applies identically to both parties; no asymmetry. AMBIGUITY 0.00: unambiguous, and the conflicts-of-laws carve-out removes the one interpretive question such clauses usually raise. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00 and ENFORCEABILITY 0.00: NOT because foreign governing law is risk-free for an Indian party, but because indian_legal_rules.csv contains no rule covering choice of law or forum. Scoring above zero here would require importing legal knowledge from outside the sanctioned inventory, which the pilot brief forbids. The concern is recorded instead as a legal-rule gap and as a POTENTIAL FUTURE LEGAL-CONTEXT NOTE (see pilot report). legal_risk_type 'jurisdictional concern' is tagged because the tag vocabulary supports it even though no numeric dimension could be scored -- this is itself a schema observation.
ai_uncertainty_note: This clause demonstrates the CUAD jurisdiction mismatch concretely: a Delaware governing-law clause is exactly what a ClauseXplain user would most want flagged, and the current Indian rule inventory is silent on it.
ai_guideline_issue: A legal_risk_type tag can be justifiably applied when every numeric dimension is 0.00. Guidelines do not address whether that combination is permitted.

clause_text: The license under this Agreement is a non-exclusive, non-assignable and non-transferable license.
annotation_notes: The clearest clause in the pilot and a useful low-risk anchor. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: all three restrictions (non-exclusive, non-assignable, non-transferable) bind the licensee only. Per the guidelines, asymmetry that is standard and expected for the clause type is not by itself unfair, so this sits at Low rather than Moderate -- but the guidelines also direct using 0.25 rather than 0.00 where SOME asymmetry exists, which it does. AMBIGUITY 0.00: three standard licensing terms of art, no undefined operative language, no cross-reference. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00 / ENFORCEABILITY 0.00: no rule applies; nothing in the text restrains trade, assigns pre-existing IP, or creates perpetual obligations. NOTE: requires_legal_review was initially drafted as False here -- this is the one clause in the pilot where an annotator would plausibly say no legal review is needed. Validation REJECTED that: PHASE2_ANNOTATION_GUIDELINES.txt requires True on every record, and the validator enforces it. Corrected to True in deference to the authoritative guidelines. Recorded as PILOT ISSUE #4 -- a field that is always True carries no information.
ai_uncertainty_note: Minimal. The span is short but complete and self-contained.

clause_text: The Owner Indemnified Parties' additional insured status will not limit the application of insurance protection as required by this Agreement which arises out of the Operator's indemnity obligations. These policies shall provide primary coverage for claims in which Operator has agreed to hold harmless and/or to indemnify the Owner Indemnified Parties.
mapping_reason: Insurance requirements concern allocation of the risk of loss between parties; grouped with Liability, though it could reasonably stand alone in a future revision.
legal_basis: ICA_S73_01 is the only Liability-scoped rule in the inventory and is rule_type=contextual (statutory default for compensation where the contract is silent). It does not address insurance or additional-insured status, so it is not cited.
annotation_notes: Insurance-allocation clause: Owner Indemnified Parties' additional-insured status is preserved alongside Operator's indemnity, and Operator's policies are primary. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: structurally favours the Owner (Operator's insurer pays first), but primary-coverage wording is conventional where one party performs operations on another's asset. AMBIGUITY 0.50: the double negative 'will not limit the application of insurance protection as required by this Agreement which arises out of the Operator's indemnity obligations' is genuinely hard to parse, and 'Owner Indemnified Parties' plus the underlying indemnity obligations are defined outside the span. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00 / ENFORCEABILITY 0.00: no rule in the inventory reaches insurance terms.
ai_uncertainty_note: Whether this clause is favourable or unfavourable depends on the indemnity obligations it cross-references, which are not in the span.
ai_guideline_issue: The Liability category's only rule is contextual and concerns damages, not insurance. Category-to-rule coverage is thinner than the category list implies.

clause_text: During the Term, CNET will not enter into more than      two other agreements under which CNET receives consideration from a      Competing Computer Products Retailer for displaying permanent links to or      other fixed promotions for such Competing Computer Products Retailer on any      CNET Site; provided that the foregoing will not restrict the display of(a)      standard advertisements for any Competing Computer Products Retailer or its      products or (b) any promotions within COMPUTERS.COM or within CNET's Snap!      Online service (which are expressly excluded from this provision).
mapping_reason: This is a carve-out/exception TO Non-Compete, Exclusivity, or No-Solicit clauses. It typically narrows or reduces restriction risk rather than increasing it. Should NOT be scored as risk-increasing merely because it shares a category with Non-Compete -- requires a separate polarity flag before any risk scoring is built on top of it.
legal_basis: ICA_S27_01 (restraint of trade) was considered and NOT applied. Its trigger_condition requires that the restriction is 'not limited to a narrow, reasonable scope'. Here the restriction IS bounded on three axes: a numeric cap (no more than two other agreements), a temporal limit ('During the Term'), and express carve-outs. Trigger not met; no rule asserted.
annotation_notes: POLARITY CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY. Phase 1 flagged CUAD 'Competitive Restriction Exception' as a risk-REDUCING carve-out wrongly grouped with risk-increasing Non-Compete. This clause shows the flag was right but incomplete: the span is BOTH at once. Its first half imposes a restriction (CNET may not enter more than two competing-retailer promotion agreements); its second half carves out standard advertisements, COMPUTERS.COM and Snap!. A single polarity label could not describe this span. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: binds CNET only, so it is one-directional -- but it is a negotiated in-term commercial cap with substantial express exclusions, not a blanket prohibition. AMBIGUITY 0.50: 'standard advertisements', 'fixed promotions' and 'permanent links' are undefined and carry real weight, since they mark the boundary between prohibited and permitted conduct. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: ICA_S27_01 trigger not met (see legal_basis). ENFORCEABILITY 0.25: residual only. Note this is an IN-TERM restriction on contracting with third parties, not a post-termination restraint on CNET's own trade; the rule's own exception_condition treats that distinction as context-dependent, and it is not resolved here.
ai_uncertainty_note: Whether an in-term exclusivity-style cap engages s.27 at all is context-dependent and the inventory does not settle it. Confidence Low.
ai_guideline_issue: A span can simultaneously restrict AND carve out. Neither the guidelines nor the schema provide a way to record mixed polarity within one record.

clause_text: Both Parties agree that during the Term of this Agreement and for a period of two (2) years following the termination, both Parties will not (i) solicit, encourage, or take any other action, which is intended, directly or indirectly, to induce any employee to terminate his or her employment with a Party; or (ii) interfere in any manner with the contractual or employment relationship between the Parties and any their employees.
legal_basis: ICA_S27_02 (rule_type=risk_trigger) applied. Its trigger_condition is that the restriction is 'broad/indefinite in scope or duration'. Duration here is definite (two years) and does NOT meet the trigger, but scope does: limb (ii) prohibits interference 'in any manner' with any employment relationship, which is open-ended in a way limb (i) is not. Applied on the scope limb only. Consistent with the rule's exception_condition, this is flagged as a matter for review rather than treated as a conclusion -- Indian courts assess reasonableness on the facts, and post-termination employee non-solicitation is treated differently from a restraint on a party's own trade.
annotation_notes: The only clause in the pilot where a rule's trigger_condition is affirmatively met, and the only Medium provisional level. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: expressly mutual ('Both Parties ... both Parties'), so the burden is symmetric -- this is why unfairness stays Low despite the restriction being substantive. AMBIGUITY 0.50: 'interfere in any manner' is vague and load-bearing; 'take any other action, which is intended, directly or indirectly, to induce' is broad; and the text contains an apparent drafting error ('between the Parties and any their employees'). NON_COMPLIANCE 0.25: partial trigger only -- scope limb met, duration limb not. Deliberately not higher, because a two-year, mutual, employee-focused non-solicit is not the paradigm s.27 case. ENFORCEABILITY 0.50: the breadth of limb (ii) is a genuine and reviewable concern, stated as a concern rather than a conclusion.
ai_uncertainty_note: The gap between limb (i) (narrow, conventional) and limb (ii) (broad) is the whole question. A human may reasonably score non_compliance 0.00 by reading the clause as a single conventional non-solicit, or 0.50 by weighting limb (ii) more heavily. This is the clause most likely to produce genuine inter-annotator disagreement.
ai_guideline_issue: No instruction exists for partial trigger satisfaction -- where a rule's trigger_condition has two limbs and only one is met.

clause_text: Any such audit will be conducted upon [*] ([*]) days notice and during regular business hours, and shall be at [*] expense, unless such audit reveals a discrepancy of more than [*] percent ([*]%) in the total applicable amount reported by HSWI, in which case [*] shall pay for, or reimburse [*] the cost of, such audit.

annotation_notes: MOST HEAVILY REDACTED SPAN IN THE PILOT. Five separate '[*]' redactions remove the notice period, the discrepancy threshold percentage, and -- critically -- the IDENTITY OF THE PARTY bearing the audit expense in each branch ('at [*] expense', '[*] shall pay for, or reimburse [*]'). UNFAIRNESS 0.25: the cost-shifting structure (auditing party pays unless a material discrepancy is found) is a recognised and reasonably balanced mechanism. But this score is close to unassessable, because which party sits on which side of the mechanism is redacted. AMBIGUITY 0.75: High. Nearly every operative variable is masked. This is the highest single dimension score in the pilot and it is driven by redaction, i.e. by a property of the SOURCE DOCUMENT, not of the underlying clause -- which the schema has no way to distinguish. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00 / ENFORCEABILITY 0.00: no rule in the inventory covers audit rights. ICA_S23_01 is the only 'Other'-scoped rule and is a general contextual validity backstop that plainly does not apply.
ai_uncertainty_note: These 0.00 scores mean 'no concern identified within the rule inventory', NOT 'assessed as risk-free'. The schema cannot currently express that difference.
ai_guideline_issue: Redaction-driven ambiguity is scored identically to drafting-driven ambiguity, which conflates a source-data artifact with a clause defect.

clause_text: Solely in the event that Dova has terminated this Agreement pursuant to Section 12.3.1 and notwithstanding anything else herein, in consideration of the promotion services performed by Valeant during the Term, with respect to the Tail Period, Dova shall make payments to Valeant in an amount equal to [***] of the amounts that would have been payable by Dova to Valeant with respect to such Tail Period pursuant to Section 6.1 had the Agreement not been so terminated.
mapping_reason: A named sum payable on breach.
legal_basis: ICA_S74_01 (rule_type=risk_trigger) was considered and NOT applied. Its trigger_condition requires a monetary sum or formula named as payable ON BREACH. On the visible text the payment trigger is Dova's own termination under Section 12.3.1, and the payment is consideration for promotion services already performed during the Term -- not a stipulated consequence of a breach by Valeant. Applying s.74 here would be exactly the 'liquidated damages = illegal penalty' error the methodology warns against. No rule asserted.
annotation_notes: CATEGORY QUESTIONABLE -- SECONDARY FINDING. CUAD labels this 'Liquidated Damages' and the mapping sends it to 'Penalties', but the text reads as a post-termination tail-compensation provision protecting the SERVICE PROVIDER (Valeant) for work performed, payable when the CLIENT (Dova) terminates. It is compensatory in direction, not punitive. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: the clause favours Valeant, and the party bearing the obligation (Dova) is the one who triggers it by its own election to terminate. Low. AMBIGUITY 0.50: the multiplier is redacted '[***]', and 'Tail Period', Section 12.3.1 and Section 6.1 are all outside the span. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: ICA_S74_01 trigger not met (see legal_basis). ENFORCEABILITY 0.25: residual only, recording that if the redacted multiplier were large enough and the surrounding sections recharacterised the payment as a consequence of breach, the s.74 question could arise. Not resolvable here.
ai_uncertainty_note: Mapping a clause to 'Penalties' predisposes an annotator toward s.74. Reading the text on its own terms points the other way. A human should confirm this reading.
ai_guideline_issue: Category assignment can prime the annotator toward a specific statutory rule. Guidelines give no instruction to read the text independently of its category label first.
